frontmatter.description: Use automatically as the sole routing entry for UI-related work. Before implementation, select the smallest useful UI skill context with the globally installed ui-skills CLI (fall back to npx ui-skills). Prefer one narrow skill, and never combine a read-only audit skill with a modifying skill in the same execution. If the registry reports an ambiguous slug, use its namespaced slug such as emilkowalski/prototype; local-only skills such as app-shell-ui must be handled explicitly.

Apply a fast spacing, hierarchy, typography, and small-layout cleanup. Use only when explicitly invoked or selected by ui-skills-root for a narrow cleanup. Do not introduce animation or replace the product's visual identity.

Audit an existing product surface against its own design evidence and write implementation plans. Strictly read-only on product source. Use only when explicitly invoked or selected by ui-skills-root, and never combine it with a modifying skill in the same execution.

Audit and fix HTML accessibility issues including ARIA, keyboard navigation, focus, contrast, and form errors. Use only when explicitly invoked or selected by ui-skills-root for an accessibility-specific task.

Audit and fix page metadata including titles, descriptions, canonical URLs, social cards, favicons, JSON-LD, and robots directives. Use only when explicitly invoked or selected by ui-skills-root for metadata, SEO, or social-preview work.

Audit and fix animation performance problems such as layout thrashing, non-composited properties, scroll-linked motion, and costly blur. Use only when explicitly invoked or selected by ui-skills-root for motion-performance work.

Create or update DESIGN.md from an existing product repository or public website. Use only when explicitly invoked or selected by ui-skills-root. Modify only DESIGN.md; do not change product source, dependencies, or configuration.

Build or restyle an explicit App Shell UI or macOS-style desktop-tool shell with shared navigation and light/dark themes. Use only when the user asks for this style or invokes the skill. Do not override an existing product identity unless the user explicitly requests it.

Apply Apple's interface and physical-motion principles to gesture, spring, drag, swipe, sheet, momentum, material, or reduced-motion work. Use only for an explicit Apple-style or gesture-driven request; do not use as a general UI-polish skill.

Build multiple genuinely different UI variants behind a visual picker for deliberate divergent exploration. Run only when explicitly invoked; do not use for routine cleanup, review, or implementation of an already chosen direction.

Choose an opinionated library for a specific frontend capability from the bundled list. Run only when explicitly invoked or when ui-skills-root selects it for a dependency-choice question; do not trigger during ordinary implementation.

Read-only search for high-confidence places where motion would help, with precise recommendations and deliberate rejection of unnecessary animation. Run only when explicitly invoked; it does not implement changes.

Read-only audit of a codebase's animation and motion, producing prioritized findings and self-contained implementation plans. Run only when explicitly invoked; never combine it with a modifying skill in the same execution.
Review a specific animation or motion change against a high craft and performance bar. Run only when explicitly invoked; do not use for general UI review, broad audits, or implementation.

emil-design-eng.reason: Overlaps the narrower animation skills and contains intrusive global response behavior. Keep its knowledge available without registering it as an active skill.
